text: Eleven blocks in the cold, and the cold got the better of the eleven blocks.

text: Between two and four there is nobody out but me and whoever is paid to be.
The sky over the river had gone grey along the bottom edge.
Shutters up, gratings back, and a man with a hose putting the night down the drain.
The El went over while I was crossing, and for twenty seconds the street had nothing to say.
A patrolman came the other way and we each decided the other was nobody.
The milk wagon had the whole block ahead of me, iron tyres on the cobbles.
The bells at the corner rang the half hour at my back.
A whistle went off the river, two long and one short, and nobody looked up.
A truck dropped the last edition at the kerb and pulled away with the doors still open.
Chairs were going up on the tables behind me before I had the door shut.
Past the corner, past the grating, past the same two men who had not moved.
